clue.text: Firm support for unoriginal performer?

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: A company props up a performer who never does anything original.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: someone who only imitates others is a kind of performer of other people's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who imitates or copies others lacks originality, so a mimic or imitator fits the description loosely.

clue.text: Arrive carrying cooking utensil and dish

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: to arrive is to come
a pot is a cooking utensil

explanation.surface: Someone turns up holding a pan and a serving dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' could be the second thing being carried; it is the definition, joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Compote is stewed fruit served in syrup, a dessert, so it is a kind of prepared food or course.

clue.text: Quality of note which cricketers need

blocks.note: first meaning: how high or low a musical note sounds
second meaning: the strip of ground where cricket is played

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one idea about a note cricketers need, but splits into two separate meanings. In cricket the pitch is the 22-yard strip between the wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both musical height of a sound and the prepared playing strip in cricket.

clue.text: Domains filling English politicians with anger

indicators.note: to fill something is to go inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
MPs are Members of Parliament
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Territories full of furious English members of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The politicians are split apart so the anger can sit inside them, with English leading.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a realm or territory ruled by a sovereign, so domains are synonyms.

clue.text: Salesperson by a street offering food

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A street vendor selling something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a street-food seller, but the salesperson is just REP.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a meal, a formal word for what is eaten at one sitting.

clue.text: Imagine not beginning tricky puzzle

indicators.note: without its start, the word loses its opening letter
something tricky is twisted and devious, so the letters get twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the word with its first letter removed

explanation.surface: Picture a puzzle that has no obvious starting point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky puzzle' looks like one phrase, but 'tricky' is the anagram signal and 'puzzle' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something baffling that needs solving.

clue.text: A national organisation associated with one cold region or another

definitions.note: read as 'the other one', the opposite polar region

blocks.note: taken as written
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage charity
the region around the North Pole

explanation.surface: A national body linked to the polar regions.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives one polar region with A and NT in front, and 'or another' points to the other pole. The National Trust is a British conservation charity owning historic houses and land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic is one frozen polar zone; the region around the South Pole is the other, so 'another' identifies it.

clue.text: Pet with brown tail mostly missing — odd

indicators.note: if most of a word goes missing, only a scrap of it is kept

blocks.note: tan is a light brown
the word with all but its first letter gone
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A strange-looking pet animal, brown, with most of its tail gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' suggests an animal, but here it means a fit of sulking. Rum as 'odd' is old-fashioned British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet in this sense is a fit of childish sulking or bad temper, the same thing as an outburst of rage.

clue.text: Angry old lover, an underground worker who wants questions answered?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the person, 'one who wants questions answered'

blocks.note: cross means angry
an ex is a former partner
an is the indefinite article, A
a miner works below ground

explanation.surface: A furious former partner, a coal miner, demanding answers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of the person rather than a noun, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In court, the lawyer questioning the opposing side's witness puts questions and insists on replies.

clue.text: Issue new item

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters come out in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Release a newly made product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a noun beside 'new item', but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something is to send it out or give it off, the verb sense of discharge.

clue.text: Not giving up with prettiness destroyed

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps going even after their good looks are ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten letters of fodder for a ten-letter answer is the giveaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent describes someone who keeps trying and refuses to stop, a direct synonym for dogged.

clue.text: Fuss when sibling loses a right

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so letters drop out

blocks.note: a brother is a sibling
R is the abbreviation for right; this letter is the one removed

explanation.surface: A family row when one brother is denied his entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A right' sounds like an entitlement, but it is just the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother is trouble, commotion or annoyance, the same sense as a fuss or to-do.

clue.text: What may be worn — more short robes, properly tailored

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the word preceding it loses its final letter
tailoring cuts and reshapes material, so the letters are refashioned

blocks.note: the word without its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: More garments, cut short and neatly tailored, ready to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short robes' looks like a phrase, but 'short' cuts the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat, a vague example of clothing that someone puts on.

clue.text: Downcast journalists probing exploit

indicators.note: to probe is to poke inside, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: the press is journalists collectively
an exploit is a feat or deed

explanation.surface: Gloomy reporters investigating somebody's exploitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' reads as a verb, but it is the noun meaning a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast and depressed both mean low in spirits, sad and dejected.

clue.text: Reason for cancelling outdoor event? Minor star is upset

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so its letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An outdoor show is called off, and the lesser celebrity is unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description, signalled by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy wet weather is a classic cause of calling off a fete, match or open-air concert.

clue.text: A male cat gets something tiny

blocks.note: taken as written
the usual name for an uncastrated male cat

explanation.surface: A tomcat is given a small treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something tiny' sounds like what the cat is given, but it defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest particle of an element, and figuratively a minute amount.

clue.text: Announcement of importance? Hang about

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: weight means importance or influence

explanation.surface: Something significant is about to be declared, so stand by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang about' is informal British English for staying put a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang about is to linger or stay put until something happens.

clue.text: Little person not getting on — we express sadness

definitions.note: a statement the answer could make about itself: 'we' are those who cry

indicators.note: not getting something means going without it, so letters are left out

blocks.note: wee is Scottish for little
the word with the two letters spelling 'on' removed

explanation.surface: A small person who can't get on in life, and so a group feels sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in the clue is the removed letters, not a link; the definition is voiced by the answer itself, as people who cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who cry show grief through tears, so a group of them could say they express sorrow.

clue.text: Stars offering old jokes on island

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one thing on another places it after, so the second-named piece goes first

blocks.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is trite or hackneyed humour

explanation.surface: Celebrities telling stale gags while on holiday on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities, but it means a constellation. In an across clue, A on B puts A after B.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn is a constellation and zodiac sign, a named group of heavenly bodies.

clue.text: Article about musical event

indicators.note: about can mean around or all over the place, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece reviewing a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article about' reads as a piece of writing on a topic; 'about' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a solo or small-group performance of music before an audience.

clue.text: Almost all of a military group in a systematic plan for living

indicators.note: almost all means everything bar the end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a regiment, without its final letter

explanation.surface: Nearly an entire army unit following a disciplined way of life.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at soldierly discipline, which fits the answer's sense neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet, exercise or treatment followed to stay healthy.

clue.text: Nervous, performing with advantage

blocks.note: a performer who is on is on stage
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: Anxious while performing, though holding the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes 'Nervous' look like a description of the performer; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense and jumpy is the idiomatic meaning of the phrase, the same as anxious.

clue.text: The fellow left to go down to island capital

blocks.note: he refers to a man
L is the abbreviation for left
to sink is to go down
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A man departs, heading down to the capital of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island capital' looks like one phrase; the island gives I and 'capital' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the chief city and seat of government of Finland.

clue.text: Alter church, leading to endless wrath

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
anger, with its final letter removed

explanation.surface: Reform the church, which provokes unending fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading to' places the church first.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to modify or make it different, a straight synonym.

clue.text: A player going down the side of the field is inspiring

blocks.note: taken as written

blocks.clueFragment: player going down the side of the field
blocks.note: in football or rugby, the player who runs along the touchline is named after that flank position

explanation.surface: A winger running down the flank is impressive to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: The long phrase is a single piece; 'inspiring' is the definition in the sense of filling with awe.
explanation.definitionFit: To awe someone is to fill them with wonder, so filling with awe is inspiring reverence.

clue.text: Unusually decent boss? Less than ideal

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters appear in an uncommon order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A surprisingly kind manager is not quite perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the wordplay; the definition follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not quite the top choice is inferior to the optimum, falling short of perfection.

clue.text: For foot one needs a doctor

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree

explanation.surface: Anyone with a bad foot should see a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The foot is not a body part but a metrical unit in poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse, a foot is a unit of rhythm; an iamb is one with an unstressed then stressed syllable.

clue.text: Tot comes with me to river when it's hot?

blocks.note: a tot is a sum added up, as in 'tot up'
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A small child joins me on a trip to the river in warm weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler, but it means an addition, a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: The warmest season of the year is the time when the weather is typically hot.

clue.text: Union Jack, maybe, on vessel

blocks.note: the Union Jack is the British flag, an example of one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Union Jack flying on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container for drink; 'maybe' marks the Union Jack as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large jug or bottle for wine or cider, a container for liquid.
